docs: SOL Bridge Lock Program
Security-critical vault program that locks SOL for cross-chain bridging
to DecentralChain. Uses PDA-controlled custody with no external key authority.
INVARIANTS:
- No SOL leaves vault without valid burn proof from DCC
- Nonces are strictly monotonic per user
- Transfer IDs are globally unique (hash of sender + nonce + slot)
- Deposits are rate-limited and size-capped
- Emergency pause halts all operations
- Reentrancy protection via Anchor's CPI guard

instructions.name: accept_authority
docs: Accept a pending authority transfer (step 2 of 2-step transfer).
Must be called by the pending authority after 24h timelock.

instructions.name: cancel_resume_request
docs: Cancel a pending resume request.
Authority or guardian can cancel — defense-in-depth.

instructions.name: close_expired_attestation
docs: Reclaim the rent of an accumulator whose transfer expired before quorum
was reached and executed. Refunds only to the recorded rent payer.

instructions.name: configure_mint_limits
docs: Create or update the per-mint SPL withdrawal limits for one mint.
Authority-gated exactly like `update_config`. Every value is in the
mint's smallest units — these limits are entirely separate from the
lamport-denominated limits on `BridgeConfig`, which govern native SOL
only. A mint with no limits account cannot be withdrawn at all.

accounts.name: bridge_config
docs: Read-only. Deliberately NOT `mut`: this instruction reads the authority
for the permission check and nothing else, so it is structurally
incapable of altering native SOL's limits or counters.

accounts.name: mint
docs: The mint being configured. Typed as `Mint` so a non-mint address cannot
be given a limits account, and pinned to `params.mint` so the account
and the PDA seed can never disagree.

accounts.name: mint_limits
docs: Per-mint limits PDA. `init_if_needed` makes this one instruction serve
both creation and update; re-initialisation is not a concern because
the authority constraint above gates every call and Anchor verifies the
discriminator and owner when the account already exists.

instructions.name: deposit
docs: Deposit SOL into the bridge vault.
Emits a BridgeDeposit event for validators to observe.

accounts.name: deposit_record
docs: Deposit record PDA — created per deposit with transfer_id seed

instructions.name: deposit_spl
docs: Deposit SPL tokens into the bridge vault.
Transfers tokens from sender's ATA to the bridge vault ATA.
Emits a BridgeDepositSpl event with the SPL mint for DCC routing.

accounts.name: deposit_record
docs: Deposit record PDA — created per deposit with transfer_id seed

accounts.name: spl_mint
docs: The SPL token mint being deposited

accounts.name: mint_limits
docs: Per-mint limits PDA (SECURITY FIX — MED-1).
WHY DEPOSITS NEED THIS. `unlock_spl` and `execute_attested_unlock_spl`
both require this exact account and fail closed without it, so a mint
with no `MintLimits` can NEVER be withdrawn. Before this constraint the
deposit side had no such requirement, so a user could send tokens into a
vault ATA they could not get back out of — inbound and outbound
disagreed about which mints the bridge supports.
Requiring it here makes the two agree: if the authority has not run
`configure_mint_limits` for this mint, Anchor aborts with
`AccountNotInitialized` before any tokens move, and the `enabled` flag
halts inbound and outbound flow for a token together.
Read-only — deposits consume no withdrawal budget, and this instruction
is structurally incapable of altering one.

accounts.name: sender_token_account
docs: Sender's token account (source)

accounts.name: vault_token_account
docs: Bridge vault token account for this specific SPL mint.
PDA-owned ATA — tokens are custodied by the bridge config PDA.

instructions.name: emergency_pause
docs: Emergency pause — halts all deposits and unlocks.

instructions.name: emergency_resume
docs: Step 2: Execute resume after the timelock delay has elapsed.

instructions.name: execute_attested_unlock
docs: Pay out native SOL against an accumulator that has reached quorum.
Permissionless — the accumulator, not the caller, authorises the payout.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: The quorum being consumed. Closed at the end of the instruction, so a
quorum can be spent at most once even before the UnlockRecord is
consulted.

accounts.name: unlock_record
docs: Replay guard — UNCHANGED from the single-transaction path. `init` fails
if this transfer_id was ever redeemed, as SOL or as SPL, by either
transport. Many accumulators may exist for one transfer_id; this makes
at most one of them payable.

accounts.name: recipient
docs: recipient — the executor cannot redirect the payout.

instructions.name: execute_attested_unlock_spl
docs: Pay out SPL tokens against an accumulator that has reached quorum.
Draws only against the per-mint `MintLimits` budget — never the
lamport-denominated counters on `BridgeConfig`.

accounts.name: bridge_config
docs: DELIBERATELY NOT `mut` — same reasoning as `unlock_spl`. Every limit and
counter on this account is lamport-denominated and belongs to the native
path. Declaring it read-only makes it structurally impossible for an SPL
withdrawal to touch `current_daily_outflow`, `total_locked` or
`total_unlocked`.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: Boxed: `AttestationAccumulator` is ~900 bytes and this context already
carries several token accounts. Heap-allocating the big ones keeps
`try_accounts` inside the BPF 4 KiB stack frame.

accounts.name: unlock_record
docs: Replay guard — SHARED namespace with native `unlock`, so one transfer_id
pays out exactly once, as SOL or as SPL, never both.

accounts.name: spl_mint
docs: Pinned to the mint the validators signed over.

accounts.name: mint_limits
docs: Per-mint withdrawal limits. The ONLY account this instruction reads
limits from and the ONLY one it writes an outflow counter to; every
field is in this mint's smallest units. Fails closed — an unconfigured
mint has no PDA here and Anchor aborts before the handler runs.

instructions.name: execute_scheduled_unlock
docs: Execute a scheduled (large) unlock after its timelock delay has elapsed.

instructions.name: initialize
docs: Initialize the bridge configuration.
Can only be called once by the deployer.

instructions.name: register_validator
docs: Register a validator's public key for signature verification.

instructions.name: remove_validator
docs: Remove a validator from the active set.

instructions.name: request_resume
docs: Step 1: Request resume — starts a timelock countdown.
The bridge remains paused until resume() is called after the delay.

instructions.name: submit_attestation
docs: ── ATTESTATION ACCUMULATOR PATH ──
Record ONE validator's attestation for one exact payout, in its own
transaction. Quorum is accumulated on-chain across several small
transactions instead of being carried inside the transaction that moves
the money, so transaction size stops scaling with `min_validators`.
This is an ADDITIONAL transport. `unlock` and `unlock_spl` are untouched
and remain fully supported; validators sign the identical canonical
message for either path.

accounts.name: bridge_config
docs: Read-only. Nothing here writes bridge state — this instruction moves no
money and touches no counter.

accounts.name: attestation
docs: The accumulator for this exact payload. Created by the first attestation,
joined by every later one.
The address is bound to BOTH `transfer_id` and `payload_hash`, and the
handler proves `payload_hash == sha256(canonical_message)`. Two
attestations therefore land in the same account only if they are
signatures over byte-identical messages.

accounts.name: validator_entry
docs: The attesting validator's registry entry. Typed and PDA-constrained, so
Anchor itself proves ownership, discriminator and derivation before the
handler runs — strictly stronger than the remaining_accounts scan the
single-transaction path has to do.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Whoever pays the accumulator's rent. Permissionless — a relayer may do
it. Rent comes back to the account recorded as `rent_payer` when the
accumulator is closed.

instructions.name: unlock
docs: Unlock SOL from the vault after validators confirm a burn on DCC.
Requires M-of-N validator signatures.

instructions.name: unlock_spl
docs: Unlock SPL tokens from the bridge vault after validators confirm a burn on DCC.
Requires M-of-N validator signatures over a mint-bound, domain-separated message.
Transfers from the bridge_config-owned vault ATA to the recipient's ATA.

accounts.name: bridge_config
docs: Global config. Read for the pause flag, chain ID and quorum size, and
used as the vault ATA's signing authority.
DELIBERATELY NOT `mut`. Every withdrawal limit on this account is
lamport-denominated and belongs to the native SOL path. Declaring it
read-only makes it structurally impossible for an SPL withdrawal to
touch `current_daily_outflow`, `total_locked`, `total_unlocked`, or any
other native counter: Anchor never serialises a non-`mut` account back,
and the runtime rejects writes to accounts not marked writable.

accounts.name: unlock_record
docs: Replay guard. `init` fails if this transfer_id was ever redeemed —
SHARED namespace with native `unlock`, so one transfer_id can be paid
out exactly once, as SOL or as SPL, never both.

accounts.name: spl_mint
docs: The SPL mint being released. Pinned to the mint the validators signed
over, so attestations cannot be redirected to a different token.

accounts.name: mint_limits
docs: Per-mint withdrawal limits (PDA: [b"mint_limits", spl_mint]).
This is the ONLY account this instruction reads limits from and the ONLY
account it writes an outflow counter to. All of its fields are in this
mint's smallest units, so no unit mixing with lamports is possible.
FAIL CLOSED: this is a required, already-initialised, typed account. A
mint the authority has not explicitly configured has no PDA here, so
Anchor aborts with `AccountNotInitialized` before the handler runs.
There is deliberately NO fallback to `bridge_config`'s native limits.

accounts.name: vault_token_account
docs: Bridge vault ATA — source of the unlocked tokens. The
`associated_token::*` constraints force this to be the canonical ATA for
(spl_mint, bridge_config); no substitute token account is accepted.

accounts.name: recipient
docs: Mirrors `unlock.rs`, which also types the recipient as a SystemAccount.

accounts.name: recipient_token_account
docs: Recipient's ATA. Created on demand so a withdrawal never fails (or
strands tokens) just because the recipient has no account for this mint.

docs: Update bridge configuration (rate limits, validator set, etc.)

types.name: AttestationAccumulator
docs: Accumulated validator attestations for ONE exact payout.
PDA: seeds = [b"attest", transfer_id, payload_hash]
WHY THE PAYLOAD HASH IS IN THE SEED.
`payload_hash = sha256(canonical_signed_message)`, and the canonical message
commits to every value that decides where money goes: the domain separator
(which distinguishes native from SPL), transfer_id, recipient, spl_mint,
amount, burn_tx_hash, dcc_chain_id and expiration. So:
* Two attestations can only land in the same accumulator if they are
signatures over byte-identical messages. Attestations for different
payouts live at different addresses and can never be summed into one
quorum.
* A single compromised validator cannot squat the address for a real
transfer_id with a bogus payload and freeze the withdrawal: their junk
accumulator lives somewhere else entirely, and the honest one is
unaffected. (Keying only on transfer_id would have made one leaked key
a permanent fund-freezing DoS.)
Uniqueness of the *payout* is still enforced where it always was — by the
`init` on the `[b"unlock", transfer_id]` UnlockRecord. Many accumulators may
exist for one transfer_id; at most one of them can ever be executed.

types.name: ConfigureMintLimitsParams
docs: Parameters for creating or updating an SPL mint's withdrawal limits.
UNITS: every amount here is in the **smallest unit of `mint`** (i.e. scaled
by 10^decimals), NOT lamports. For USDC (6 decimals), 50,000 USDC is
50_000_000_000. These values are never compared against, added to, or
derived from any lamport-denominated field on `BridgeConfig`.
── HOW THE THREE CAPS RELATE (read before setting them) ───────
They are not independent, and the SPL path does NOT behave like the native
SOL path here. `unlock_spl` and `execute_attested_unlock_spl` enforce:
amount <= max_unlock_amount            (else UnlockAmountExceeded)
amount <  large_withdrawal_threshold   (else UnlockAmountExceeded)
running daily total <= max_daily_outflow
The native path SCHEDULES a withdrawal at or above its threshold; the SPL
path REJECTS one, deliberately, because a deferred SPL record would sit in
the shared `[b"unlock", transfer_id]` namespace and be payable in lamports
by `execute_scheduled_unlock` (see the deviation note in `unlock_spl`).
So the largest SPL withdrawal that can ever succeed is
`min(max_unlock_amount, large_withdrawal_threshold - 1)` — and an operator
who mirrored the live native numbers, where `max_unlock_amount ==
large_withdrawal_threshold`, would set a cap that is unreachable by exactly
one base unit, with nothing on chain explaining the rejection (AUDIT-2).
The handler now REFUSES that configuration:
`max_unlock_amount < large_withdrawal_threshold` is required, which makes
`max_unlock_amount` the true, reachable, per-transaction cap and
`large_withdrawal_threshold` a strictly higher hard stop. Set the threshold
deliberately above the cap — e.g. cap 10,000 USDC, threshold 10,001 USDC —
rather than copying the native config.

fields.name: large_withdrawal_threshold
docs: Withdrawals at or above this size are hard-rejected (smallest token
units). Must be strictly ABOVE `max_unlock_amount`, so it is a backstop
rather than the real limit.

types.name: MintLimits
docs: MINT LIMITS — Per-SPL-mint withdrawal circuit breaker
Per-mint withdrawal limits (PDA: seeds = [b"mint_limits", mint])
WHY THIS EXISTS — UNIT SAFETY.
Every limit field on `BridgeConfig` (`max_daily_outflow`,
`current_daily_outflow`, `max_unlock_amount`, `large_withdrawal_threshold`)
is denominated in **lamports**. SPL amounts are raw base units of an
arbitrary-decimal mint, so they are not comparable to lamports and must
never be added into the same counter: 50,000 USDC is 5e10 base units, which
would consume the entire 50 SOL (5e10 lamport) native daily budget in one
withdrawal and freeze native SOL withdrawals for 24 hours.
Every field below is denominated in **the smallest unit of `mint`**, and
this account is the ONLY place `unlock_spl` reads or writes withdrawal
limits. There is exactly one of these per mint, so one token's activity can
never consume another token's budget, and no token's activity can ever
consume native SOL's budget.

fields.name: mint
docs: The SPL mint these limits govern (must equal the PDA seed).

fields.name: max_daily_outflow
docs: Maximum daily outflow for this mint (smallest token units) — circuit breaker

fields.name: current_daily_outflow
docs: Current window outflow for this mint (smallest token units) — resets daily

fields.name: max_unlock_amount

fields.name: large_withdrawal_threshold
docs: Threshold at or above which a withdrawal of this mint is rejected
outright (smallest token units). SPL withdrawals are never scheduled —
see the deviation note in `unlock_spl::handler`.

fields.name: enabled
docs: Whether withdrawals of this mint are permitted at all. Lets the
